name: og-30-spatially-integrated-protometabolism
title: Spatially Integrated Protometabolism
claim: The full vent-fed chemical network, placed in an explicit mineral pore with reactive transport, thermophoresis and surface adsorption, either sustains productive reaction flux that EXCEEDS a matched well-mixed control AND a matched nonconcentrating control — demonstrating that the pore itself helps — or it does not, in which case the clean result is that pores do not help under these conditions. Spatial benefit is a margin won against controls, not assumed from co-localization.
question: Can the full chemical network operate productively inside a pore despite fractionation and washout — and does the pore structure actually improve persistence over a well-mixed system?
hypothesis: Reactive multispecies transport with thermophoretic accumulation and mineral-surface adsorption will co-localize intermediates and raise local productive flux and residence time enough to beat both a matched well-mixed control and a matched nonconcentrating control; if co-localization does not produce a flux margin over those controls, the pore confers no benefit and that is reported.
objective: Run the 29 reaction network inside an explicit mineral-pore transport field (FiPy), with thermophoresis and surface adsorption, using discrete stochastic chemistry where molecule counts make a continuum unreliable; quantify co-localization, spatial reaction flux, residence and persistence against matched well-mixed and nonconcentrating controls.
proposed_mechanisms: thermophoretic / gradient-driven accumulation of intermediates in the pore
mineral-surface adsorption concentrating and positioning reactants
washout vs residence as the competition that determines persistence
proposed_models_methods: FiPy finite-volume multispecies reactive transport                      [in-workspace: viva_genesis.transport]
multispecies-reactive-transport cross-solver comparison                 [to-build: adds an independent solver check]
mineral-surface adsorption / evolving catalytic accessibility           [to-build: mineral-surface-dynamics]
discrete/stochastic chemistry where expected counts make continuum unreliable (evidence standard #7) [in-workspace/partial: continuum-stochastic handoff is to-build]
PHREEQC speciation coupling for pore chemistry                          [wrapper-needed: viva_phreeqc]

model_approach.prose: Study 30 puts the chemistry of study 29 into space. The pore is not assumed to help: the whole point is the two matched controls. A well-mixed control runs the identical network with the identical input fluxes but no spatial structure; a nonconcentrating control keeps the geometry but removes the accumulation mechanism. Only productive flux (and persistence) that beats BOTH counts as a spatial benefit. Where expected molecule counts in a pore subvolume are small, the chemistry is simulated with discrete kinetics rather than continuum concentrations, so accumulation is not an artifact of treating a few molecules as a smooth field.

gate_B: Gate B (spatial organization) = Gate A + study 30 passing together. Acceptance REQUIRES that explicit mineral pores improve productive network persistence over BOTH the well-mixed and the nonconcentrating matched controls with input fluxes held equal.
decision_test: Productive flux must EXCEED a matched well-mixed control AND a matched nonconcentrating control (chemical input fluxes held equal) over the transport/residence timescale. A clean negative — pores do not help — is an accepted result, reported not tuned (evidence standard #5, #7, #8).

config.title: Does the pore help? Enrichment, residence, and flux vs control
config.caption: Thermophoretic enrichment factor and residence time in the structured pore, then net productive carbon flux in the pore against a matched well-mixed control at identical feeds. Plainly: the pore gathers and holds the ingredients — but the real test is whether that makes more product than a stirred pot, shown in the third panel.

key_assumptions: Two adverse controls are required — a well-mixed control and a nonconcentrating control — both matched on feed, network and total material.
Where molecule counts are low, continuum concentrations are unreliable and discrete stochastic chemistry is used instead.
expert_questions: What count threshold should trigger the continuum-to-stochastic handoff, and which species most need it?
